prompt: An editable JComboBox keeps the five most recent searches, newest first, with case-insensitive de-duplication. Complete record(term) so blank and null terms are ignored and the cap is never exceeded.
explanation: A DefaultComboBoxModel supports insertElementAt and removeElementAt, which is what lets you push a term onto the front instead of appending it. Removing the old match before inserting is what makes a repeat search move to the top rather than appear twice, and equalsIgnoreCase is what makes "JAVA" and "java" count as the same search. Enforcing the cap with a while loop after the insert keeps the rule in one place no matter how many entries were already stored.
hints: Guard null first, then trim, then guard the empty string -- three early returns before any model work.
Search for an existing match with equalsIgnoreCase and remove it before inserting the new term at index 0.
After inserting, use a while loop that removes the last element while getSize() is greater than MAX_ENTRIES.
